subject: Re: SLO derogation & monitoring runbook - PrimeBio
messages:
From: Liam Carter <liam.carter@primebio.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Srivastava <priya@primebio.com>
Date: 2028-11-01T16:12:00Z
Subject: Request: Private VPC SLO derogation for PrimeBio production

Marcus —

Thanks for taking the call today. As discussed, PrimeBio is deploying Redwood Private into our primary production VPC but we have a set of legacy edge appliances (third-party WAN accelerator + NAT gateway) that the networking team controls. Over the past quarter we observed short-lived egress disruptions and long tails (200-400ms) from our on-prem NAT during peak backup windows; those events are outside of Redwood's control but they materially affect p95 latency and appear in customer-facing monitoring.

We want to propose an SLO derogation for the private deployment so that Redwood's uptime/latency guarantees exclude 'customer-managed egress tail events' provided we meet these conditions:
- PrimeBio exposes VPC flow logs and a single support VPN for full-packet traces on request
- PrimeBio implements the active probes (ICMP/tcp/latency synthetic) described in the attached vpc-handback-proposal-2028-11-01.pdf
- Mutually agreed incident evidence window of 15 minutes where PrimeBio proves the event originated on its edge devices

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept an exclusion clause like this and what operational commitments Redwood would require (instrumentation, retention of logs, notification windows)?

I'll attach an excerpt of the network trace (edge-network-trace-2028-10-28.pcap) that shows the tail behavior.

—Liam
Liam Carter
Director of Infrastructure | PrimeBio
liam.carter@primebio.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Liam Carter <liam.carter@primebio.com>
Cc: Priya Srivastava <priya@primebio.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-01T20:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: Private VPC SLO derogation for PrimeBio production

Thanks Liam — good writeup and thanks for the packet capture. We can accommodate an exclusion for customer-managed edge-induced latency tails, but we'll need a short set of operational guardrails to make it fair to both sides. High-level proposed approach: 

1) Evidence and instrumentation
- PrimeBio must enable VPC flow logs and provide either S3 access or weekly exports so Redwood can correlate ingress/egress windows.
- Active probe configuration: 1s pings from two Redwood probe subnets to a PrimeBio probe endpoint, plus tcp-based latency checks to the public load balancer.
- When an exclusion is invoked, PrimeBio provides the 15-minute capture window and mark the timestamps in the flow logs.

2) Exclusion language (draft)
- \"For Private/VPC deployments where the Customer maintains control over network egress, Redwood's availability and latency SLOs shall exclude periods where the Customer demonstrates, by mutually agreed evidence (VPC flow logs, packet captures, active probe traces), that the root cause resides on Customer-controlled network appliances or transit.\"

3) Operational commitments from Redwood
- Redwood will provide a runbook template and a run-of-record for requests (SERV-712).
- Retain correlated SLO evidence for 90 days for dispute resolution.
- Provide a one-hour initial acknowledgement for any exclusion requests and a 48-hour joint analysis window.

4) Fallbacks and mitigations
- If prolonged edge instability can be demonstrated (>6 hours in 24h reporting window), Redwood will offer a temporary routing fallback to a hosted proxy variant (subject to capacity) and a proportional credit calculation described in the attached PDF.

I'll loop in Vanessa (Support) and Kim (Legal) to validate the wording and confirm whether the 90-day evidence retention and 48-hour analysis window are acceptable from our side.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Liam Carter <liam.carter@primebio.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-02T14:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: Private VPC SLO derogation for PrimeBio production

On Thu, Nov 1, 2028 at 08:03 PM Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> I'll loop in Vanessa (Support) and Kim (Legal) to validate the wording and confirm whether the 90-day evidence retention and 48-hour analysis window are acceptable from our side.

Thanks — quick note from Support ops: the 48-hour joint analysis window is tight if we need packet-forensics, but acceptable as long as PrimeBio provides S3 access to the flow logs and a named contact who can retrieve packets on demand. A couple clarifications: 
- We need the customer to tag suspected exclusion windows in their ticket and provide the trace id in the first 8 hours. This prevents stale evidence requests.
- For the temporary hosted-proxy fallback, Redwood will only move traffic if the customer consents to a short-term configuration change; that change must be included in a signed change-control.

Operational ask: can PrimeBio include the IP ranges of the on-prem appliances in the initial handback doc? That will speed triage.

Vanessa Ortiz
Support & Escalations Manager | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
From: Liam Carter <liam.carter@primebio.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Srivastava <priya@primebio.com>, PrimeBio Procurement <procure@primebio.com>
Date: 2028-11-03T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: Private VPC SLO derogation for PrimeBio production

On Fri, Nov 2, 2028 at 06:28 PM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com> wrote:
> Operational ask: can PrimeBio include the IP ranges of the on-prem appliances in the initial handback doc? That will speed triage.

Yes — attached is the handback proposal with IP ranges and the active-probe endpoints. We accept the 48-hour joint analysis window and the 90-day evidence retention. Procurement copied here — we'd like the exclusion to be codified in the Master Services Agreement as an Exhibit B (SLO exclusions for customer-managed egress).

Two small asks from PrimeBio: 
1) We need the exclusion to be applied retroactively to the Oct 28 event so it doesn't count against Redwood's Q4 availability heatmap while we formalize the clause. We'll provide packet captures and flow logs within 24 hours.
2) Can Redwood commit to an SLA credit cap during fallback (so we know exposure)?

Attaching: vpc-handback-proposal-2028-11-01.pdf, edge-network-trace-2028-10-28.pcap

—Liam
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Liam Carter <liam.carter@primebio.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-07T22:46:00Z
Subject: Re: SLO derogation & monitoring runbook - PrimeBio

On Mon, Nov 3, 2028 at 10:05 AM Liam Carter <liam.carter@primebio.com> wrote:
> We'd like the exclusion to be codified in the Master Services Agreement as an Exhibit B... and retroactively apply to Oct 28.

Thanks, Liam — appreciate the clarity and the packet capture. Legal has reviewed and we can accept the proposed Exhibit: we recommend the following final points before execution:

- Retroactive application: Redwood will treat the Oct 28 event as an exclusion upon receipt and verification of the 15-minute evidence window (PCAP + flow logs). Credits will not be applied for that event.
- Evidence handling: PrimeBio grants Redwood read-only S3 access to exports for the verified windows; Redwood will not store raw PCAPs beyond the 90-day evidence retention period.
- Credit cap during fallback: During any hosted-proxy fallback period, SLA credits are capped at 15% of the affected monthly plan invoice.
- Change control: Any traffic routing change to enable hosted-proxy fallback requires written approval from PrimeBio's engineering lead; Redwood will not implement routing changes unilaterally.

Next steps: 
1) I'll attach a redline of Exhibit B and circulate the final MSA packet to procurement (HubSpot deal RB-PRIME-2028-042).
2) Marcus/Vanessa — please prepare the runbook template (SERV-712) and the probe config snippets.
3) Liam/Priya — please confirm S3 export access and the initial evidence upload timeline.

If all good, Procurement and Legal can sign the exhibit and we'll close this out.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
